plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit positions in weak semiconductor (MUU) and software leverage (PLTU, METU).
Reduce QQQI concentration to 20% to manage risk.
Buy XLF to add diversified financial exposure.

Expect a lower target return with a focus on minimizing drawdowns.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for capital preservation with a target monthly return around 1.5%. It significantly reduces leverage and focuses on stable assets, aiming for low drawdowns. Expect slower growth compared to other modes.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to maintain limited exposure.
Reduce positions in weaker semiconductor (MUU) and software leverage (PLTU, METU).
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration.
Buy ASML to add a high-quality semiconductor name.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
Targeting around 2.5% monthly return with moderate risk.
balanced.read: This balanced strategy targets approximately 2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding quality names. It aims for risk-first growth, accepting moderate drawdowns for potential gains. Cash buffer is around 10%.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and specific tech names (MUU, PLTU, METU).
Trim QQQI to 15% to allow for concentration in higher-conviction plays.
Buy TSLA as a high-potential growth addition.
This aggressive plan aims for high growth by concentrating leverage.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk and leverage decay.
aggressive.read: This aggressive strategy targets ~4% monthly return by concentrating leverage in high-conviction tech and leveraged ETFs. It accepts significantly higher potential drawdowns and the risk of leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is paramount.

moves.note: Reduce broad index for income focus

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta single names (CRWD).
Exit volatile semiconductor (MUU) and software leverage (PLTU, METU) positions.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
Trim SPY to 10% to prioritize monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly income.
Expect low drawdowns and reliable, though variable, income distributions.
income.read: This income-focused strategy prioritizes steady monthly distributions with a target of ~1% monthly return. It eliminates leverage and volatile assets, focusing on income ETFs like QQQI. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
